source: hand-authored K/1/2/4 practice item banks (science, social_studies, ela-story) — factual recall MC, options 3-6, correctIndex valid; mirrors the existing content.json bank-mode generator item shape

letter-sounds.question: Which letter makes the sound at the START of "map"?
letter-sounds.hint: The first sound you hear in map is /m/.

letter-sounds.question: What sound does "t" make at the start of "top"?
letter-sounds.hint: t makes a quick tap sound /t/.

letter-sounds.question: Which letter is the FIRST letter in the word "sun"?
letter-sounds.hint: Read the word from left to right; the first letter is s.

letter-sounds.question: Which of these starts with the letter "b"?
letter-sounds.hint: b says /b/, and bat begins with /b/.

letter-sounds.question: Rhyming words share the same ENDING sound. Which pair rhymes?
letter-sounds.hint: Rhyme check: do they end in the same sound?
letter-sounds.praise: Yes - cat and hat both end in -at.

story-questions.question: Who is the story about? (a boy named Sam who lost his hat)
story-questions.hint: The main character is the one the story follows.
story-questions.praise: Yes - the story is about Sam.

story-questions.question: What did Sam lose in the story?
story-questions.hint: Look for the thing Sam could not find.

story-questions.question: Where did Sam look for his hat?
story-questions.hint: Find the place Sam checked first.
story-questions.praise: Yes - he looked under the bed.

story-questions.question: What happened at the END of the story?
story-questions.hint: The ending tells what was solved.
story-questions.praise: Yes - Sam found his hat in the end.

story-questions.question: Why was Sam sad at the start?
story-questions.hint: The problem is what makes the character sad.
story-questions.praise: Yes - losing his hat made Sam sad.

story-questions.question: How did Sam feel when he found the hat?
story-questions.hint: Finding something lost usually makes you happy.

weather-patterns.question: What do we use to check the weather outside?
weather-patterns.hint: You look outside to see the weather.

weather-patterns.question: Which of these is a sunny-day sign?
weather-patterns.hint: Sunny days have bright sun and blue sky.

weather-patterns.question: What might you need when it rains?
weather-patterns.hint: An umbrella keeps you dry in the rain.

weather-patterns.question: Is it cold or hot on a snowy day?
weather-patterns.hint: Snow only falls when it is cold.

weather-patterns.question: What season has the warmest, sunniest days?
weather-patterns.hint: Summer has the longest, hottest days.

weather-patterns.question: We record the weather each day in a...
weather-patterns.hint: A chart helps you track daily weather.

classroom-rules.question: Why do we have rules in the classroom?
options: So everyone is safe and can learn
classroom-rules.hint: Rules keep things fair and safe for learning.
classroom-rules.praise: Yes - rules help everyone learn safely!

classroom-rules.question: What should you do when the teacher is talking?
classroom-rules.hint: Listening shows respect and helps you learn.

classroom-rules.question: How should you take turns with materials?
classroom-rules.hint: Taking turns is fair to everyone.

classroom-rules.question: What is a fair way to solve a disagreement?
options: Use kind words and take turns
classroom-rules.hint: Kind words fix problems better than yelling.

classroom-rules.question: Why must we raise our hand to speak?
options: So everyone gets a turn to talk
classroom-rules.hint: Raising your hand gives each person a fair turn.
classroom-rules.praise: Yes - raise your hand for a turn.

classroom-rules.question: What do we do with toys when the lesson ends?
classroom-rules.hint: Cleaning up keeps the room ready for the next activity.

sound-vibration.question: What makes a drum make sound when you hit it?
sound-vibration.hint: Sound starts when something shakes back and forth - that is vibration.

sound-vibration.question: Which of these can you HEAR?
sound-vibration.hint: You hear sounds with your ears.
sound-vibration.praise: Yes - you can hear a bell ring.

sound-vibration.question: What do your vocal cords do when you speak?
sound-vibration.hint: Your throat vibrates to make your voice.

sound-vibration.question: Where do the vibrations from a guitar string go?
options: Into the air as sound waves
sound-vibration.hint: Vibrations travel through the air as sound.
sound-vibration.praise: Yes - sound waves in the air!

sound-vibration.question: Why does a spoon make noise when you tap a bowl?
sound-vibration.hint: Tapping makes the bowl shake - vibrate - and that is sound.

sound-vibration.question: What happens to sound if you cover your ears?
sound-vibration.hint: Covering ears blocks some sound waves.

light-and-sight.question: What do you need to SEE an object?
light-and-sight.hint: You need light to reflect off things so your eyes can see them.

light-and-sight.question: What makes a shadow?
light-and-sight.hint: When an object blocks light, the dark spot behind it is a shadow.

light-and-sight.question: Which of these gives off its OWN light?
light-and-sight.hint: The sun makes its own light; the moon only reflects it.

light-and-sight.question: Why can you not see in a perfectly dark room?
options: There is no light to reflect
light-and-sight.hint: No light = nothing for your eyes to catch.

light-and-sight.question: What do mirrors do with light?
light-and-sight.hint: Mirrors reflect light like a bounce.

light-and-sight.question: You can see a ball in a dark room if you...
light-and-sight.hint: Add light and the ball becomes visible.
light-and-sight.praise: Yes - shine a light on it!

sky-patterns.question: What do we see in the daytime sky?
sky-patterns.hint: The sun is up during the day.

sky-patterns.question: When do we usually see the moon?
sky-patterns.hint: The moon shines in the night sky.

sky-patterns.question: Which star is closest to Earth?
sky-patterns.hint: The sun is our nearest star.
sky-patterns.praise: Yes - the sun is a star!

sky-patterns.question: What changes make the seasons?
options: How Earth is tilted as it orbits the sun

sky-patterns.question: Which season has the longest days?
sky-patterns.hint: Summer has the most daylight hours.

sky-patterns.question: What pattern do the sun and moon follow?
options: They rise and set each day/night
sky-patterns.hint: Daily rise-and-set is the basic sky pattern.

classroom-rules.question: Why does our class have rules?
options: To keep everyone safe and learning
classroom-rules.hint: Rules protect safety and focus for learning.

classroom-rules.question: What should you do before speaking in class?
classroom-rules.hint: Raising your hand gives everyone a fair turn.

classroom-rules.question: How do you show respect for a classmate’s idea?
classroom-rules.hint: Listening and taking turns shows respect.

classroom-rules.question: What is the fair way to share supplies?
classroom-rules.hint: Sharing fairly means everyone gets a chance.

classroom-rules.question: Why do we clean up after an activity?
options: So the next group is ready
classroom-rules.hint: Cleaning up keeps the room ready for the next class.
classroom-rules.praise: Yes - so the next group is ready.

classroom-rules.question: What should you do if you disagree with a rule?
options: Raise your hand and ask respectfully
classroom-rules.hint: Ask respectfully - that is how fair rules get discussed.

material-properties.question: Which material is the HARDEST?
material-properties.hint: Hard materials keep their shape and do not squash easily.

material-properties.question: Which material lets light pass through?
material-properties.hint: Transparent materials like clear glass let light through.

material-properties.question: What property describes how heavy something is?
material-properties.hint: Mass tells you how much matter is in an object.

material-properties.question: Which material is the BEST insulator (keeps heat in)?
material-properties.hint: Wool traps air and slows heat loss.

material-properties.question: A material that bends easily without breaking is...
material-properties.hint: Flexible things bend; rigid things do not.

material-properties.question: Which is a NATURAL material?
material-properties.hint: Wood comes from trees - it is natural.

plants-need-sun-water.question: What do plants need to make their own food?
plants-need-sun-water.hint: Plants use sunlight + water to make food (photosynthesis).

plants-need-sun-water.question: Why do plants need water?
plants-need-sun-water.hint: Water keeps plants growing and healthy.

plants-need-sun-water.question: What gas do plants take in for photosynthesis?
plants-need-sun-water.hint: Plants breathe in CO2 and breathe out oxygen.

plants-need-sun-water.question: What do plants release as a product of photosynthesis?
plants-need-sun-water.hint: Plants give off oxygen - we breathe it!

plants-need-sun-water.question: Where do most plants grow best?
plants-need-sun-water.hint: Soil anchors roots; sunlight powers growth.

plants-need-sun-water.question: What happens to a plant with no water for a long time?

land-and-water.question: What is LAND?
land-and-water.hint: Land is solid ground - soil, rock, grass.

land-and-water.question: What is WATER (on a map)?
land-and-water.hint: Water features are blue on most maps.

land-and-water.question: What can slowly change the shape of land?
land-and-water.hint: Erosion from water and wind reshapes land over time.

land-and-water.question: Which is a large body of salt water?
land-and-water.hint: Oceans are the biggest salt-water bodies.

land-and-water.question: Where does a river usually END up?
land-and-water.hint: Rivers flow downhill to lakes or oceans.

land-and-water.question: What is a hill?
options: A piece of land higher than the ground around it
land-and-water.hint: Hills rise above the surrounding land.

local-government.question: What does local government DO?
local-government.hint: Local government runs the town: laws, roads, safety.

local-government.question: Who helps keep a town safe every day?
local-government.hint: Local safety services protect the community.

local-government.question: What is an ORDINANCE?
local-government.hint: Ordinances are laws passed by a town or city.

local-government.question: Where do town leaders meet to make decisions?
local-government.hint: City or town hall is the seat of local government.

local-government.question: Why do towns make rules (ordinances)?
options: To keep people safe and orderly
local-government.hint: Rules keep a community safe and running smoothly.

local-government.question: Which of these is a LOCAL service?
local-government.hint: Trash pickup is a town-provided service.

energy-and-motion.question: What is ENERGY?
options: The ability to do work or cause change
energy-and-motion.hint: Energy powers all motion and change.

energy-and-motion.question: The FASTER an object moves, the more it has...
Energy stored for later use is called...
energy-and-motion.hint: Potential = stored, ready to be released.

energy-and-motion.question: In a collision, what usually happens to energy?
options: It transfers from one object to another
energy-and-motion.hint: Energy is transferred, not created from nothing.

energy-and-motion.question: A heavier object at the same speed has...
energy-and-motion.hint: More mass at same speed = more kinetic energy.

energy-and-motion.question: What happens to total energy in a closed system?
energy-and-motion.hint: Conservation of energy: total stays constant.

waves-sound-light.question: What is a WAVE?
waves-sound-light.hint: Waves move energy from place to place.

waves-sound-light.question: WAVELENGTH is the distance between...
options: Two matching points on a wave

waves-sound-light.question: Sound waves travel best through...
waves-sound-light.hint: Sound needs a medium - solids/liquids work well.

waves-sound-light.question: Light waves can travel through...
waves-sound-light.hint: Light needs no medium - it crosses empty space.

waves-sound-light.question: A longer wavelength of visible light looks more like...
waves-sound-light.hint: Red has the longest visible wavelength.

rocks-and-fossils.question: What do FOSSILS tell scientists?
rocks-and-fossils.hint: Fossils are preserved remains of ancient life.

rocks-and-fossils.question: Most fossils are found in...
rocks-and-fossils.hint: Sedimentary rock forms in layers where organisms get buried.

rocks-and-fossils.question: Rock layers (strata) are usually...
options: Oldest on the bottom, youngest on top

rocks-and-fossils.question: What process slowly WEATHERS rock?
rocks-and-fossils.praise: Yes - water, wind, ice over time!

rocks-and-fossils.question: EROSION is when weathered material is...
rocks-and-fossils.hint: Erosion transports weathered bits to new spots.

rocks-and-fossils.question: Which is NOT a type of fossil?
options: A footprint in a computer chip
rocks-and-fossils.hint: Real fossils are preserved remains/imprints, not electronics.
rocks-and-fossils.praise: Yes - computer chips are not fossils!

michigan-inquiry.question: What do historians ASK when studying Michigan?
options: Why did events happen and how do we know?
michigan-inquiry.praise: Yes - why and how, with evidence!

michigan-inquiry.question: What is a PRIMARY source?
options: A document/artifact from the time being studied
michigan-inquiry.hint: Primary = created at the time, first-hand.

michigan-inquiry.question: What is a SECONDARY source?
options: Something written AFTER the event using primary sources

michigan-inquiry.question: Which is a good question for studying Michigan’s past?
options: How did the Great Lakes shape trade and towns?
michigan-inquiry.hint: Good historical questions are about patterns over time.
michigan-inquiry.praise: Yes - lakes shaping trade and towns!

michigan-inquiry.question: Where do historians find EVIDENCE?
michigan-inquiry.hint: Evidence lives in real documents and artifacts.

us-regions-maps.question: A LEGEND (key) on a map tells you...
The UNITED STATES is commonly divided into...
us-regions-maps.hint: Common regional groupings split the country.

us-regions-maps.question: What are PUSH factors in migration?
options: Reasons to LEAVE a place (conflict, jobs)

us-regions-maps.question: What are PULL factors in migration?
options: Reasons to GO TO a place (jobs, safety)

us-regions-maps.question: A compass rose shows...
us-regions-maps.hint: The compass rose is the direction guide.
